newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat says settlements "basic issue" blocking peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says settlements "basic issue" blocking peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said Israel's construction of Jewish settlements was a main issue behind the current deadlock, which U.S. and European Union envoys will try to break, in Middle East peace negotiations.
He was speaking to reporters in Cairo late on Sunday after arriving for talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, whom he consults regularly.
"The Judaisation of Quds (Jerusalem) is a dangerous crime as well as continued action to confiscate land and build settlements, especially Jabal Abu Ghneim," Arafat said.

"This is the basic issue between us and them, in addition to lack of accurate and honest implementation of what has been agreed upon, whether it be the first, second or third peace agreements signed in Washington or Cairo."
Israeli-Palestinian negotiations were broken off after Israel started to build on a Jewish settlement on a site in East Jerusalem called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.
Israel regards East Jerusalem as part of its indivisible capital, Palestinians view it as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
EU envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos arrived in Cairo on Sunday and Arafat is to meet Israeli President Ezer Weizman on Tuesday.

Asked if he thought U.S. envoy Dennis Ross, due in the region on Monday, had new ideas to break the stalemate in peace talks, Arafat said: "I don't think so." But he added: "All of our options are open."

"The problems which we face and which obstruct the peace process are from the Israeli side, foremost of which are the settlements, especially Jabal Abu Ghneim, as well as not implementing the agreements," he said.
Palestinian minister Nabil Shaath, who accompanied Arafat, said there was a crisis of trust over cooperating with Israel on security.

Palestinian officials have said they suspect Israeli secret services of operating in self-rule areas and Shaath was asked about a Palestinian who said he was recruited by Israel to incite Moslem militants to carry out two suicide attacks which killed the bombers.

Israel described the allegation was "a ridiculous lie," but Shaath said: "This is a very serious matter. We have revealed full information that the two so-called operations...were actually conducted by the Israeli Shin Bet."

"This I think sheds a great light on the whole campaign of (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin ) Netanyahu to paint the Palestinians as organising terror, giving green light to terror. Terror was actually fabricated by the Israelis," he told Reuters television.
"This also increases our feeling of lack of trust as to the Israeli call for security coordination. What they want is actually creating disturbances that can be blamed on the Palestinians."
